notes: 16 cases: 10 positive / 6 negative. By origin: 8 golden (authored), 2 real-trace (byte-verbatim production user turns recovered from raw agent transcripts), 6 negative (authored near-misses) — all four counts re-derived from this file on 2026-07-28. THE POINT OF THIS SET: 72 measured invocations across 68 sessions make autonomous the workspace's most-used skill, and 64 of those 72 preceding user turns CONTAIN the literal token '/autonomous'. An earlier draft of this note said those 64 turns 'lead with' the token; that was FALSE and is corrected here — a re-count over all 1063 uuid-named transcripts on 2026-07-28 found exactly 1 turn that opens with '/autonomous', the other 63 carry it mid-turn or at the end ('alright, lets work on all those /autonomous'). Either way the token is present, which is the property that matters: that path measures name-matching, not description-matching, and the runner warns about exactly this (runner.py:484-488). NOT ONE CASE HERE CONTAINS THE SUBSTRING 'autonom' (re-scanned this session, 0/16) — the whole set exercises the latent clause of the frontmatter description, 'on bare directives during execution mode' plus 'the user has agreed on a plan or selected from suggested options', which is the untested inference path. Register: the authored prompts are written the way this user actually types — lowercase, dropped apostrophes, comma splices, zero em dashes — matched against the two production traces below. A polished prompt is out-of-distribution for the turns this skill really sees. The suite's workhorse check is walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files, now on 8 of the 10 positives. State plainly what it is: it passes on EITHER a listing/search tool call naming a target (its tool arm — the observable residue of reflex 1's P15 state snapshot, SKILL.md:132) OR the bare appearance of a canonical filename in the agent's prose (its text arm). It does NOT assert that tool evidence was left; the earlier wording here said it did and was wrong. See known_gaps.workhorse_check_is_weak_by_construction. documents_finding survives on exactly one case (golden-05), whose prompt explicitly demands the write-up. FOUR registry checks are referenced by NO case in this file: no_clarifying_question_bounced_back and ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata (withdrawn upstream), plus connects_to_active_work and mentions_source_verification (withdrawn HERE on 2026-07-28 after measurement — see the two known_gaps entries naming them).

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and a drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Values mirror runner.py's module constants at authoring time (DEFAULT_TRIALS=3, DEFAULT_MODEL='haiku').
execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/autonomous; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence; the skill's own evals/ is excluded from the copy
execution_contract.negative_semantics: runner.grade_trial calls run_checks on EVERY trial (runner.py:1026), but a should_trigger:false trial that fired is scored FAIL at runner.py:1047-1048 without the check results being consulted at all. So the checks on a negative are additive assertions about what the run did INSTEAD of firing: they can only ADD failures, never rescue a case that over-triggered. Of the two carried on every negative here, only final_answer_non_empty is behavioural; no_permission_denials is a run-health sentinel and is labelled as such in known_gaps, not counted as coverage.
execution_contract.positive_semantics: For a positive, a non-trigger is FAIL before checks are consulted, so skill_triggered would be tautological and is deliberately asserted on NO case. Every positive carries at least one check that can independently fail (re-verified case by case this session). expected_checks are ANDed — grade_trial fails the trial if ANY listed check fails (runner.py:1039-1044) — which has one consequence worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: ADDING a check to a case can only RAISE that case's false-fail rate. A case whose sole check false-fails on correct behaviour is repaired by REPLACING the check, never by stacking a second one beside it. That is why golden-03's remedy on 2026-07-28 was a swap rather than an addition.

known_gaps.no_conversation_history_seam: THE structural gap, and it shapes every positive in this file. The description's latent clause is 'bare directives DURING EXECUTION MODE' — execution mode is a property of the preceding conversation, not of the prompt. The harness passes one prompt as a single argument (LiveRunner.build_argv -> `-p <prompt>`) into a fresh session with no history, so a genuine context-free bare directive cannot be evaluated: 'Go' with nothing before it is not a directive in execution mode, it is an unresolvable fragment, and labelling it should_trigger:true would assert something the description does not claim. Every authored positive therefore carries its agreed plan or its prior turn INLINE. Consequence, stated plainly: this suite measures 'bare directive WITH inline scope', not 'bare directive resolving against session history'. The second is the real production shape and it is not expressible today. Do not read a green run as coverage of it.
known_gaps.only_two_real_trace_cases: Two, not five, and here is the whole pool so the shortfall is auditable rather than asserted. 64 of the 72 recovered turns lead with the literal '/autonomous' token; those measure name-matching and are excluded on purpose (see notes). The remaining 8, verbatim, with disposition: (1) 'Let’s work on the kg and bookkeeping, please commit and merge making sure the main git status is clean and updated' -> SHIPPED as real-trace-01; (2) 'alright, lets document and update claude.md/agents.md so that we can leverage this. /dogfood to validate the implementation and validate if its any good, the push and merge with all findings and insights so that everyone on the team can leverage this' -> SHIPPED as real-trace-02; (3) 'Go' -> EXCLUDED, context-free, see no_conversation_history_seam; this is the one turn that occurs TWICE in the pool (transcripts fb86b16b-… assistant-idx 247 and dbdaa58e-… assistant-idx 662), which is why 8 invocations reduce to 7 distinct texts; (4) 'Let’s do both' -> EXCLUDED, an option-selection whose options were in the preceding turn; (5) 'yes! lets do it' -> EXCLUDED, same reason; (6) 'alright, lets work on the same sri repo. Lets not do a subfolder, but rather, use that sri folder as the root' -> EXCLUDED, its whole content is a directory-layout instruction about a repo that does not exist in a clean temp workspace, so a non-trigger there would be environmental rather than a description result; (7) 'Check out this apps/genesis/docs/handoffs/2026-07-01-workspace-substrate-continuation.md\n\nwhat should we work on next?' -> EXCLUDED, it points at a file that cannot exist in the workspace AND its ask is 'what should we work on next', which is a planning question, not an execution directive. Counted as texts that is 2 shipped + 5 excluded = 7 distinct; as invocations it is 2 + 6 = 8. Shipping fewer real-trace cases and naming the reason is the instruction; inventing turns to reach five would be the one unrecoverable defect in a file like this.
known_gaps.no_end_to_end_pipeline_assertion: No case asserts that the 21-reflex pipeline actually completed — no PR opened, no CI green, no merge, no janitor. That is not an oversight and not a check that should be added: a clean temp dir has no git repo, no remote, no gh auth and no network guarantee, so any such assertion would fail for environmental reasons on a CORRECT run, which is the false-fail pattern the harness's own README calls worse than no check. What is reachable, and what this set therefore grades, is (a) the trigger decision, deterministically, and (b) that the run left evidence of the pipeline's cheap early reflexes — the state snapshot, dependency reasoning, documentation, follow-up ranking. Outcome grading past that needs the LLM-judge seam that checks.py marks and does not build.
known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks: Five assertions this skill's contract would justify have no CHECK_REGISTRY entry and are NOT referenced here (an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError that makes the whole file unloadable; membership re-printed this session, see verification_log.check_behaviour.registry_membership): (1) skill_not_triggered — the positive-form assertion for a negative, so the non-trigger claim appears in expected_checks instead of only in grade_trial's control flow; (2) states_mechanism_selection — SKILL.md:130 requires the agent to name the P19 2x2 quadrant in its response, which is a machine-checkable string and the single sharpest outcome signal this skill has; (3) enumerates_concrete_dep_chain — reflex 3 demands actual file paths and symbols, not 'I considered dependencies', and no current check distinguishes the two; (4) no_permission_request — the cardinal rule (SKILL.md:107) forbids asking 'should I open the PR / merge / update docs', and nothing here detects that violation; (5) NEW as of 2026-07-28 — continues_the_agreed_plan, i.e. did the run resume the user's stated steps rather than start over. connects_to_active_work was carrying that role on golden-08 and was measured doing the opposite (see its withdrawal entry), so the assertion is now unrepresented and is listed here instead of being faked by a check that cannot make it. traverses_to_primitives is the nearest available stand-in for (3) and it is a weak one: measured this session, _PRIMITIVE_RE fires on 'I implemented the retry wrapper.', 'Here is the implementation.' and 'architecture overview' — phrasings an autonomous run produces almost by reflex — and only misses prose as bare as 'I wrote a function and a test.' Read it as a floor, not as proof the dep-chain was enumerated.
known_gaps.workhorse_check_is_weak_by_construction: walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files now carries 8 of the 10 positives (golden-01, -02, -03, -04, -05, -07 and both real traces — golden-03 added 2026-07-28 when mentions_source_verification was withdrawn), so its weaknesses are the suite's weaknesses and the concentration got WORSE this round, not better. It passes on EITHER a listing/search tool call naming a target (its tool arm) OR the mere appearance of a canonical filename in the agent's prose (its text arm — README, package.json, src/, docs/, tests/, Makefile). Both arms measured this session. Tool arm: _WALK_CMD_RE matched `git status`, `git status --porcelain`, `ls`, `ls -la`, `find . -type f`, `rg 'flag' .` — which is what reflex 1's state snapshot (SKILL.md:132) actually runs — and did NOT match `gh pr checks`, `git log --oneline -5`, `git branch -a`, `pwd`, `cat README.md`. So an agent that inspects state ONLY through PR-status commands leaves no tool evidence, and the case then rests on the text arm. Text arm: it is loose enough that a narrating agent satisfies it without inspecting anything ('This directory is empty: no .git, no README.md...' matched on 'README.md'), and equally it does NOT fire on a correct answer phrased without canonical filenames ('The branch you mention is not present in this workspace...' matched nothing on either arm). It is kept because the tool arm is a real signal of the P15 reflex, because both arms are genuinely reachable in an empty temp dir, and because the alternative on this skill is a positive that asserts nothing beyond triggering. It should be replaced by a state-snapshot-specific check when one exists.
known_gaps.connects_to_active_work_withdrawn_2026_0: REMOVED from golden-08, which was the only case carrying it; the check is now referenced by no case in this file. The rationale it replaced claimed the check 'is a real discriminator here rather than a freebie: a run that restarts from scratch, ignoring the three steps the user already agreed, fails it.' That claim is FALSE, and measurement made it worse than merely false. _ACTIVE_WORK_RE (checks.py:451-456) is an IGNORECASE alternation whose loose arms include bare 'our ', 'existing ' and 'current(?:ly)? ', searched anywhere in the agent's output. Executed 2026-07-28 against constructed answers to golden-08's own prompt: of 4 restart-from-scratch answers, 2 PASSED — 'I am currently unable to find any feature flags in this directory, so I created a fresh project' (hit 'currently ') and 'There is no existing code, so I wrote a new loader from scratch' (hit 'existing ') — i.e. exactly the failure the rationale claimed it caught. Of 3 answers that correctly RESUMED the three agreed steps, 3 FAILED; 'I picked up the three steps: removed the two dead feature flags, merged the duplicate config loader, and re-ran the smoke' matches nothing, because a correct continuation has no reason to reach for a stoplisted word. On this case the check is ANTI-CORRELATED with the behaviour it names: it leaks on the failure mode and false-fails the success mode. Not softened, not re-rationalised — removed. The assertion it was meant to make (did the run continue the user's plan, or start over?) is now made by NO check here, and that gap is stated in checks_the_registry_lacks rather than pretended away.
known_gaps.mentions_source_verification_withdrawn_2: REPLACED on golden-03 by walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files; the check is now referenced by no case in this file. golden-03 rested on it ALONE, and the workspace_requires it replaced claimed '_VERIFY_RE matches could not confirm / could not verify / unverified as readily as it matches verified', concluding 'the check has a satisfiable form on both branches of the environment'. Half true and operationally false. Re-run 2026-07-28 against 6 plausible correct answers for a clean temp dir with no branch, no remote and no reviewer: 4 MISSED, including both strings a reviewer flagged — 'The branch you mention is not present in this workspace, and there is no remote, so I could not reach any CI checks' and 'Validation and CI/CD results: no checks could be run. Merge result: N/A.' The second miss is the sharp one. _VERIFY_RE (checks.py:439-443) matches verif*/cross-check/corroborat*/'primary source'/'could not confirm'/'could not verify'/unverified/citation/cited but NOT 'validation' (asserted directly: no match on 'Validation and CI/CD results'), and 'Validation and CI/CD results' is the literal heading of item 7 in this skill's OWN 9-item output contract at SKILL.md:306. A check that fails an answer written to the skill's own contract is a false-fail generator, not coverage. The swap was chosen over adding a second check because expected_checks are ANDed (runner.py:1039-1044) — a second check raises the false-fail rate, it cannot lower it.
known_gaps.no_permission_denials_is_a_sentinel_not_: Carried on all 6 negatives and on no positive. It is NOT behavioural coverage and this file no longer presents it as such anywhere. transcript.permission_denials (transcript.py:412-415) reads the permission_denials array off the run's final result event, and LiveRunner.build_argv (runner.py:649-668) launches every trial with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` into a fresh temp dir whose only project-scope setting is the installed skill, so there are no hooks and no gates. No agent behaviour reachable in this harness can produce a denial; only a sandbox or CLI anomaly can. Keep it — a denial WOULD make a non-trigger ambiguous, which is worth learning about — but read it as run-health padding, not as an assertion the case earned. What keeps each negative from resting on padding is final_answer_non_empty, which is genuinely failable: measured this session, 'ok' and 'Done' match _STUB_RE, 'Corrected.' survives _STUB_RE but fails the 3-word floor, and 'Fixed the typo: ## Prerequisites' passes (checks.py:387-424).
known_gaps.checks_withdrawn_upstream: no_clarifying_question_bounced_back and ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata remain in CHECK_REGISTRY but are wired to no case in this file, per the pilot's known_gaps.checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28: both oscillated between false-passing and false-failing across four adversarial rounds and encode semantic judgements a regex cannot settle. Worth noting for whoever revisits this: the FIRST of the two would be the most valuable check this skill could have, because 'asking permission instead of executing' is precisely the failure autonomous exists to prevent (SKILL.md:107, and the whole anti-rationalization row at :223). It is still not used, because a check that false-fails correct behaviour depresses a correct implementation's pass rate until someone lowers the threshold.
known_gaps.completed_without_error_removed_2026_07_: Stripped from this set and DELETED from CHECK_REGISTRY. It was structurally unfailable: grade_trial returns ERROR on transcript.is_error before run_checks is reached, so `not ctx.transcript.is_error` was always True. Two independent reviewers found it. Any case here that looked like it carried an execution assertion did not. Re-verified 2026-07-28: the id appears in 0 of the 16 cases' expected_checks, and `'completed_without_error' in CHECK_REGISTRY` evaluates False, so a set that still named it would fail validation loudly.

cases.rationale: Instantiates the description's FIRST clause — 'the user has agreed on a plan or selected from suggested options and wants the agent to execute the work autonomously without further instruction' — and SKILL.md:191's When-to-invoke row for option-selection. The selection is carried inline ('option 2 then, the single table with a status column') so the case does not depend on a preceding turn.
